# cmux-claude — agent install & operate runbook

> Executable notes for an AI agent (Claude Code, etc.) installing and driving this
> workflow on a user's macOS machine. The human-facing overview is in README.md; this
> file front-loads the non-obvious traps that otherwise cost an agent several
> round-trips. Everything here is idempotent and safe to re-run. Substitute the user's
> real paths for `$HOME`; never hardcode a password.

## Preflight (check these first — each is a silent failure otherwise)

- **macOS only.** cmux is macOS-only; `install.sh` exits on other platforms.
- **bash 4+ required to run `install.sh`.** It uses `declare -A` (associative arrays),
  which stock macOS bash 3.2 does not support — `./install.sh` dies with a parse error.
  Fix: `brew install bash` and run it under that (`/opt/homebrew/bin/bash ./install.sh`),
  or, if you can't install bash, source the helpers directly under bash and call the
  per-component installers (they don't all need associative arrays).
- **Run the installer under bash, not zsh.** `lib/common.sh` relies on `$BASH_SOURCE`
  to resolve its own directory; sourced from zsh that's unset and every symlink it
  creates silently dangles. Always `bash install.sh`, never `zsh`/`sh`.
- **jq is required** (role-injection hook + settings.json merge); `node` only for
  Micromanage's dashboard, `python3` only for Todo's.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MarcelSmuts/cmux-claude.git && cd cmux-claude
bash install.sh --micromanage --planner --todo   # or bare `bash install.sh` for the checklist
```

Components symlink into `~/.claude/` (so a later `git pull` here updates them — the
clone is load-bearing, don't delete it) and the shared `SessionStart` role hook is
merged into `~/.claude/settings.json` (pre-existing file backed up to
`settings.json.pre-cmux-claude.bak`).

## Socket control — REQUIRED for an agent to drive cmux (spawn/tell/pin)

Creating and pinning standing tabs from a script means talking to cmux's Unix control
socket. An agent shell (e.g. Claude Code's Bash tool) runs **without**
`CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID`, so cmux treats it as external and the default `cmuxOnly` mode
rejects it. You must enable password mode AND give the app a stored password to match:

```bash
# 1. Back up, then set mode + password in the config file (NOT just the Settings UI).
cp ~/.config/cmux/cmux.json ~/.config/cmux/cmux.json.bak.$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)
# edit ~/.config/cmux/cmux.json -> automation: { socketControlMode: "password", socketPassword: "<pw>" }
cmux reload-config          # app re-reads the file; no restart needed

# 2. Expose the same value to any external/agent shell, then verify.
export CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD="<pw>"
cmux ping                   # expect: PONG
```

Why the config file and not only Settings → Automation: a password set through the UI
can be **cleared by a cmux app update/restart**, after which password mode is still on
but there is nothing to match, so *every* external CLI call fails with
`Password mode is enabled but no socket password is configured in Settings.` Keeping
`socketPassword` in `cmux.json` means `cmux reload-config` re-establishes it any time.
CLI auth precedence: `--password` > `$CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD` > password saved in
Settings. The workflow scripts (`spawn`/`tell`/`sessions`/`att`/`unspawn`) pick up
`$CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD` from the environment automatically.

## Standing tabs from the CLI

`install.sh` offers to create the tabs interactively, but an agent can also do it
directly — and must, when driving a non-interactive setup:

```bash
# A named tab IN PLACE (no throwaway worktree) — the right shape for a standing tab.
# The tab title triggers the SessionStart role hook, which injects roles/<slug>.md.
bash ~/.claude/scripts/spawn.sh PLANNER     --dir "$HOME/path/to/project"
bash ~/.claude/scripts/spawn.sh TODO        --dir "$HOME"
bash ~/.claude/scripts/spawn.sh MICROMANAGE --dir "$HOME"
```

Pin each tab (so it survives and stays in the bar):

```bash
# Resolve the workspace ref by title, then pin. You MUST pass --workspace context:
# `--action pin --tab tab:N` on its own returns `not_found` (tab:N is scoped to a
# workspace). Passing --workspace lets cmux resolve that workspace's tab.
cmux workspace list --json | jq -r '.workspaces[] | "\(.ref)\t\(.custom_title)"'
cmux tab-action --action pin --workspace workspace:2   # repeat per tab
```

Two things that will otherwise mislead you:

- **`pinned` in `cmux workspace list` JSON is NOT the tab pin.** cmux has two pin
  concepts: the horizontal-tab pin (`tab-action pin`, what standing tabs use) and the
  sidebar workspace-**group** pin (`cmux workspace-group pin`, the only RPC-level
  `*.pin` method). The `pinned` field reflects the group one, so it reads `false` even
  for a correctly tab-pinned tab. To confirm a tab pin, rely on the `OK action=pin`
  response, not that flag.
- **The `micromanage` role is missing from the repo.** `install/install_micromanage.sh`
  links `roles/micromanage.md`, but that file doesn't exist upstream, so the link
  dangles and the MICROMANAGE tab loads no role. If the user wants that standing tab,
  create a real `~/.claude/roles/micromanage.md` (not a symlink into the clone) — model
  it on `roles/planner.md` / `roles/todo.md`.

## Multiple / named planners

More than one planner can run at once, each anchored to its own repo/topic. Open one
without leaving the shell (Shell integration installed):

```bash
planner viz ~/path/to/project   # opens tab "PLANNER: viz" in that repo, on the planner model
```

The role hook slugifies the title and looks up `roles/<slug>.md`; when a qualified title
like `PLANNER: viz` has no exact `roles/planner-viz.md`, it **falls back to the part
before the first `:`** (`roles/planner.md`) and tells the session its qualifier ("viz").
So one `roles/planner.md` serves every `PLANNER: <name>` tab, and a hand-written
`roles/planner-viz.md` still overrides it for that one tab. This prefix fallback is
generic — any `ROLE: qualifier` title works, not just planners.

`spawn` records which tab spawned each worker in
`~/.config/cmux-claude/spawn-owners.tsv` (`<branch>\t<owner-title>\t<utc-ts>`). From a
planner tab, `sessions.sh --mine` lists only that planner's own workers; plain
`sessions.sh` lists every tab with an `OWNER` column. `unspawn` drops the row.

## Customizing roles without dirtying the clone

`~/.claude/roles/*.md` are symlinks into this clone, so editing one in place makes the
clone dirty and will conflict on the next `git pull`. To customize per-project, replace
the symlink with a real copy, or add a per-tab-title `roles/<tab-title>.md` real file.

## Troubleshooting (symptom → cause → fix)

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install.sh`: `declare: -A: invalid option` / parse error | stock macOS bash 3.2 | run under bash 4+ (`brew install bash`) |
| Every symlink dangles after install | installer sourced from zsh (`$BASH_SOURCE` unset) | re-run with `bash install.sh` |
| `Password mode is enabled but no socket password is configured in Settings.` | password mode on, app has no stored password | set `automation.socketPassword` in `cmux.json` + `cmux reload-config` |
| `Access denied` / `Authentication required` from an external shell | agent shell isn't authing | `export CMUX_SOCKET_PASSWORD=…` (matches `cmux.json`) |
| `spawn`/`tell` say cmux is unreachable but the app is open | socket auth rejected, not a down app | same as the two rows above (this is what `sc_require_cmux` now distinguishes) |
| `cmux tab-action --action pin --tab tab:N` → `not_found` | `tab:N` needs a workspace context | add `--workspace workspace:N` |
| MICROMANAGE tab loads no role | `roles/micromanage.md` missing upstream | create a real `~/.claude/roles/micromanage.md` |

## Key paths

- cmux config: `~/.config/cmux/cmux.json` — `cmux settings path` prints all locations;
  `cmux reload-config` reloads it (and Ghostty config) with no restart.
- Installed pieces: `~/.claude/{scripts,roles,skills}/` (symlinks into this clone).
- Role hook: `~/.claude/scripts/session-role.sh`, registered as `SessionStart` in
  `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- Orchestration scripts: `~/.claude/scripts/{spawn,tell,sessions,att,unspawn}.sh` — each
  has a usage header; `sc_require_cmux` in `session-lib.sh` is the socket preflight.
